title: Media uploads
content:
# Media uploads

Upload an image, video or document with a presigned URL and attach it to a post with mediaItems.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

Upload a file (up to 5 GB) to storage through a presigned URL and attach it to a post. Files already on public HTTPS skip the upload ([requirements](#how-it-behaves)).

## Before you start

You need an API key and an `accountId` ([quickstart](/quickstart)). 3 calls:

1. `POST /v1/media/presign`
2. A `PUT` of the file
3. `POST /v1/posts` with the returned `publicUrl` in `mediaItems`

## Get an upload URL

Call `POST /v1/media/presign` with `filename` and `contentType`. Pass `size` in bytes to check the 5 GB limit before you upload.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data: presigned } = await zernio.media.getMediaPresignedUrl({
  body: {
    filename: 'photo.jpg',
    contentType: 'image/jpeg'
  }
});

const { uploadUrl, publicUrl } = presigned;
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
import httpx
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

presigned = client.media.get_media_presigned_url(
    filename="photo.jpg",
    content_type="image/jpeg"
)

upload_url = presigned["uploadUrl"]
public_url = presigned["publicUrl"]
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/media/presign" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "filename": "photo.jpg",
    "contentType": "image/jpeg"
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`200`):

```json
{
  "uploadUrl": "https://<bucket>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/temp/1234567890_abc123_photo.jpg?X-Amz-Signature=...",
  "publicUrl": "https://media.zernio.com/temp/1234567890_abc123_photo.jpg",
  "key": "temp/1234567890_abc123_photo.jpg",
  "expiresIn": 3600
}
```

- **`uploadUrl`**: valid for `expiresIn` seconds (1 hour).
- **`publicUrl`**: the address the post uses.

## Upload the file

`PUT` the file to `uploadUrl` with the same `Content-Type`. It goes to storage, not the API, so no `Authorization` header.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const fileBuffer = await readFile('photo.jpg');

await fetch(uploadUrl, {
  method: 'PUT',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'image/jpeg' },
  body: fileBuffer
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
with open("photo.jpg", "rb") as f:
    httpx.put(upload_url, content=f.read(), headers={"Content-Type": "image/jpeg"})
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
# UPLOAD_URL is the uploadUrl from Step 1
curl -X PUT "$UPLOAD_URL" \
  -H "Content-Type: image/jpeg" \
  --data-binary @photo.jpg
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Storage answers an empty `200` with an `ETag` header, never JSON. The file is now at `publicUrl`.

## Attach it to a post

Call `POST /v1/posts` with `publicUrl` in `mediaItems`. `type` is `image`, `video`, `gif` or `document`, inferred from the file extension when omitted.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data: created } = await zernio.posts.createPost({
  body: {
    content: 'Golden hour at the pier.',
    mediaItems: [
      { url: publicUrl, type: 'image' }
    ],
    platforms: [
      { platform: 'linkedin', accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d' }
    ],
    scheduledFor: '2027-01-01T12:00:00',
    timezone: 'America/New_York'
  }
});

console.log(created.post._id);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
created = client.posts.create_post(
    content="Golden hour at the pier.",
    media_items=[
        {"url": public_url, "type": "image"}
    ],
    platforms=[
        {"platform": "linkedin", "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d"}
    ],
    scheduled_for="2027-01-01T12:00:00",
    timezone="America/New_York"
)

print(created["post"]["_id"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/posts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "content": "Golden hour at the pier.",
    "mediaItems": [
      { "url": "https://media.zernio.com/temp/1234567890_abc123_photo.jpg", "type": "image" }
    ],
    "platforms": [
      { "platform": "linkedin", "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d" }
    ],
    "scheduledFor": "2027-01-01T12:00:00",
    "timezone": "America/New_York"
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "message": "Post scheduled successfully",
  "post": {
    "_id": "65f1c0a9e2b5af0012ab34cd",
    "status": "scheduled",
    "scheduledFor": "2027-01-01T17:00:00Z",
    "mediaItems": [
      { "url": "https://media.zernio.com/temp/1234567890_abc123_photo.jpg", "type": "image" }
    ],
    "platforms": [
      { "platform": "linkedin", "status": "pending" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Send different media to one platform

`mediaItems` attaches to every platform in the request. Set `customMedia` on one entry to replace it for that platform.

```json
{
  "content": "Same text, different media per platform",
  "mediaItems": [{ "url": "https://media.zernio.com/temp/1234567890_abc123_photo.jpg", "type": "image" }],
  "platforms": [
    { "platform": "linkedin", "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d" },
    {
      "platform": "instagram",
      "accountId": "66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2e",
      "customMedia": [{ "url": "https://media.zernio.com/temp/1234567890_abc123_square.jpg", "type": "image" }]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Google Drive links

A Google Drive share link works anywhere a post takes a media URL: `mediaItems[].url`, `customMedia`, `thumbnail`, `instagramThumbnail` and covers such as TikTok's `video_cover_image_url`.

Zernio copies the file into its own storage when the post is created or updated, so every platform downloads it from Zernio, never from Drive. Files too large for Drive's virus scan work too.

- **Share the file publicly.** In Drive open **Share** and set **General access** to **Anyone with the link**. A private, deleted or unknown file gets a `400` (`invalid_field_value`) on the create or update request, before any post is saved.
- **Up to 5 GB.** A larger Drive file gets a `400`. If Google Drive does not answer within 15 seconds, or the copy stalls for 30 seconds or runs past 4 minutes, the request gets a `503` (`temporarily_unavailable`) with `Retry-After` and nothing is saved: retry it.
- **Accepted links:** `drive.google.com/file/d/{id}/view`, `drive.google.com/open?id={id}`, `drive.google.com/uc?id={id}` and `drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id={id}`. A folder link gets a `400`. Google Docs, Sheets and Slides links are not media files.
- **Private files:** connect the Google account and send `{ "fileId": "...", "accountId": "..." }` in place of `url` ([Google Drive files](/platforms/google/files)).
- **Check a link first** with `POST /v1/tools/validate/media`: it inspects the file behind the share link.

## How it behaves

- **Uploads expire after 7 days.** A post created or updated with the `publicUrl` copies the file to permanent storage, so posts scheduled or queued months ahead keep their media. In a team where the team or any profile uses [zero content retention](/security/zero-content-retention), an upload is single use: it is deleted once a post or email uses it, or after 1 day unused.
- **`mediaItems[].url`** must be public HTTPS and return the file itself. Dropbox, OneDrive and iCloud links return an HTML page platforms cannot fetch. **Test a URL** in an incognito window: a webpage means the post will fail. Google Drive share links are the exception, see [Google Drive links](#google-drive-links).
- **`contentType`** must be a MIME type the [presign endpoint](/media/get-media-presigned-url) accepts (table below).
- **Audio** has no `mediaItems[].type`, so no posts. Send its `publicUrl` as `attachmentUrl` with `attachmentType: "audio"` on [send inbox message](/messages/send-inbox-message).
- **Size.** Presign caps every type at 5 GB, none smaller. Platforms are stricter (a LinkedIn document: PDF, 100 MB or less); count, size, duration and aspect ratio limits are under "Media requirements" on each [platform page](/platforms).
- **Compression.** Images and videos above a platform's limit are compressed; videos over 200 MB may not be. Bluesky images are recompressed under its 1 MB blob limit.
- **Custom thumbnail** in `mediaItems[].thumbnail` (JPG or PNG, 10 MB max): Facebook video posts, Facebook Reels, YouTube videos and LinkedIn video posts.

| Type | Formats |
|------|---------|
| Images | JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP |
| Videos | MP4, MPEG, MOV, AVI, WebM, M4V |
| Documents | PDF (LinkedIn only) |
| Audio | MP3, M4A, AAC, OGG, WAV, WebM |

## If it fails

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `400` on `POST /v1/media/presign` | Missing `filename`, unaccepted `contentType` (such as `application/octet-stream`), or `size` above 5 GB. | Send the file's real MIME type (`image/jpeg`, `video/mp4`, `application/pdf`). |
| `400` on `POST /v1/posts` | `type` contradicts the file extension. | Fix or omit `type`. |
| `400` creating a scheduled, queued or `publishNow` post | Upload older than 7 days. With zero content retention: older than 1 day, or already used by another post or email. A draft saves, but scheduling or publishing it returns `400`. | Re-upload; create the post within that window. |
| `PUT` refused by storage | `uploadUrl` older than 1 hour. | Request a new one. |

Example `400` from presign:

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid contentType",
  "type": "invalid_request_error",
  "code": "invalid_field_value",
  "param": "contentType"
}
```
